content:
Perception is Reality - Maersk & Hoegh Earnings 
Marhelm Feb 8 

This morning $MAERSK reported weak 4Q numbers, which was expected given the timing of the Red Sea disruption and the timing of the impact to rates. However, to the surprise of Wall Street, management released a muted 2024 guidance, sending the stock down 16%.

Leading Wall Street equity analyst Omar Nokta of Jefferies in a follow-up note to clients described the situation as "not wanting to come across as “profiteering” off of the Red Sea situation". 

Maersk has been at the forefront of the Red Sea news cycle, as the first major carrier to announce publicly that they would divert vessels from the area. Then issuing a public reversal on Christmas Eve, likely at the urging of Western governments following the announcement of Operation Prosperity Guardian. After one of their ships was targeted with separate missile attacks in two days, they re-announced their plan to cease all transit through the area, driving many other shipowners to follow. 

Omar went on to discuss his disagreement with their top-line EBITDA estimate of $6Bn, stating that it "seems impossible to have $6bn be the top-end if Red Sea disruptions persist all year, especially given where rates are".

But in 2024, perception is reality, and Reuters followed with the headline that management likely wanted. 

Car carrier $HAUTO announced earnings today. They too had put out a press release in January that also highlighted "the negative financial effects of rerouting vessels via Cape of Good Hope will persist into Q1". 

However, earnings today showed the ongoing strength in car carrier market as Chinese car exports have grown rapidly. 

Norwegian bank Pareto's research team, led by Eirik Haavaldsen who is regarded to be one of the top shipping analysts, put out a morning note to clients highlighting the NOK 20 dividend as "equal to a 19% yield in a single quarter (!)" The stock reacted positively, up 15% in trading today in Oslo. 

The Red Sea remains highly impacted and uncertainty remains regarding a future cease-fire in Gaza as well as Houthi activity in the area. The equities remain volatile across sectors, a bit of the tail wagging the dog, but as we progress firmly into Q1 - rates remain strong across sectors.
